name: Movement Guide rules
note: Figures the Movement Guide (MS/Engines/MovementGuide) reads. Each block carries a basis: R = a rule written in OCOKA_Roadmap.md from the Pakistan Army pamphlets (IC / IBB; cite the page before relying on it), E = an estimate or proposal by the developer, to be corrected by the user. Distances in ground metres. Movement planning and charting (march table, packets, timings) are on hold and not read from here.

basisCodes.R: rule from OCOKA_Roadmap.md (pamphlet figure, page to be cited)
basisCodes.E: estimate / proposal, for the user to correct

vp.rule: Where a convoy is likely to be hit: culverts, defiles, bridges, cuttings.

ambush.rule: Defile or bend, target hidden from following vehicles, covered withdrawal, away from reinforcements; vehicles cannot leave the road; covered fire positions beside it; no village nearby.
ambush.layoutRule: R: line, L or V layout; meeting point 750-900 m back. E: killing zone 150 m, stop groups 100 m beyond each end, target hidden from the vehicles 300 m behind.

mine.rule: Likely mine sites: crossroads, turning places, places where vehicles slow.

block.rule: Road block and tank ambush: round a bend or over a crest, no bypass, no room to turn, tied to natural obstacles.
block.estimates: E: approach watched 800 m back, no room to turn = NO-GO both sides for 150 m, sites 400 m apart, flanking positions 150 / 300 / 500 m off the road seeing 30 % or more of the approach.

convoy.rule: Packets of 5-10 vehicles, up to 5 min apart, bounds of 10-15 km, likely ambush sites cleared first.
convoy.speedNote: Speeds and halts from MovementSpeeds.json columns.wheeled (open column 40 km/h by day, 8-16 km/h blackout at night; 15 min halt every 2 h).

patrol.rule: Night routes avoid wood edges, villages, tracks and skylines; route out differs from route in. Legs, bounds and FMP from the Platoon Guide patrol card (PlatoonDoctrine.json).

infil.rule: Lanes through gaps in dead ground, off roads; objective within one night's march; the mirror: anti-infiltration posts.
infil.estimates: E: a band 1.5 km either side of the line, posts see 1.5 km at night from 3 m, the cost multipliers.

picket.rule: Pickets on both sides, spaced so fire covers the ground between; a platoon each.

checkPost.rule: Junctions that cannot be bypassed (network, NO-GO flanks).

cordon.rule: 15 men per 100 m facing inward, +5 for rooftops, +2-3 per side road; outer cordon of road blocks on every exit; rural: sections on escape routes only.

hides.rule: Caves, deserted sites, forest and broken ground near an incident.

lane.rule: Lanes through gaps in dead ground, off roads; objective within one night's march (15 km in hills, 24 km at most).

water.rule: Type of water obstacle and its main characteristics (IBB Annex P to Section 47, p463-466): dammed river, undammed river, irrigation, link, feeder and twin canals, drain, anti-tank ditch, defence drain, double ditch; home bank against far bank.
water.src: IBB Annex P, p463-466 (PDF p483-486). Feet converted at 0.3048.

dammedRiver.label: Dammed river
dammedRiver.dry: Water belt negligible, depth varies; crossable at most places. The flow can be raised from the dams to suit operations.
dammedRiver.wet: Rain, nullahs and water released from the dams turn it into a substantial obstacle.
notes: Bridges and crossing sites exist.
Ground beside it reclaimed: crops and planted trees.
Old flood bunds may stand away from the river where its course has moved.

undammedRiver.label: Undammed river
undammedRiver.dry: Wet span over 500 ft (152 m), depth varies.
undammedRiver.wet: Wider and deeper than in the dry season.
notes: Sandy bed, marshy ground astride.
Flood bunds give good observation.
Crossed at the bridges and ferry sites.
Wild growth, elephant grass common; going poorer than a dammed river.

irrigationCanal.label: Irrigation canal
irrigationCanal.dry: Runs full: 5,000-10,000 cusecs for the major canals; width and capacity fall toward the tail.
irrigationCanal.wet: As in the dry season; seepage marsh spreads.
notes: Major canals 200-300 ft (61-91 m) wide at the head.
At least one bank has a service track and embankment: vehicles on it are seen from far.
Rail, road and cattle bridges; SWR (steel wire rope) ferries.
Trees on the banks give cover.
Seepage makes marshy patches along the canal.

distributary.label: Distributary / minor (irrigation canal, tail)
distributary.src: IBB Annex P p464 s3 (width and capacity fall toward the tail)
distributary.dry: Smaller channel off an irrigation canal.
notes: Wade or bridge at a low bank; check the width first.

linkCanal.label: Link canal
linkCanal.wet: Rain water from the land drains into it.
notes: Road and rail bridges and a few others linking main towns.
Wild trees and shrubs only.
Less seepage than an irrigation canal.
The pamphlet's sketch: water deep below high spoil banks.

feederCanal.label: Feeder canal
feederCanal.dry: Over 2,000 cusecs, constant until it starts feeding other canals; 8-10 ft (2.4-3.0 m) deep.
notes: May have the character of an irrigation or a link canal.
Wild trees and shrubs.

twinCanal.label: Twin canal
twinCanal.dry: Two parallel canals very close to each other (irrigation, feeder, or one of each).
notes: Bridges for main roads and railways; others depend on the canals.
Planted trees likely.
Going as for the other canals.

drain.label: Drain
drain.dry: No flowing water outside the rains; going good.
drain.wet: Flows in the rains; going poor in the low wet patches during and after.
notes: Runs through populated areas; road, rail and village bridges.
Little vegetation.

atDitch.label: Anti-tank ditch
atDitch.dry: Dry or stagnant water; the bed is boggy. Not connected with any water source.
atDitch.wet: As in the dry season, boggier.
notes: Far bank at ground level; the spoil raises the home bank 5-10 ft (1.5-3.0 m).

defenceDrain.label: Defence drain
defenceDrain.dry: Water can be fed into it in the dry season.
notes: Far bank at ground level; home bank raised 11-15 ft (3.4-4.6 m), regular shape and constant height, for observation and defence positions.
Tracks for vehicles behind the home bank; a limited number of bridges for the defender.
The ground in front may be planned for inundation.

doubleDitch.label: Double ditch
doubleDitch.dry: An anti-tank ditch and a defence drain, or two defence drains; stagnant water, or fed in an emergency.
notes: Each about 100 ft (30 m), or one 20-30 ft (6-9 m) and the other about 100 ft.
8-10 ft (2.4-3.0 m) deep; far bank at ground level, the middle bank 2-3 ft (0.6-0.9 m) higher, the home bank as a defence drain's.
Extensive defence works on the home bank; tracks behind it; few bridges; inundation possible in front.

stream.label: Perennial stream / nala
stream.dry: Flows all year; depth and banks vary.

nala.label: Nala / dry riverbed
nala.dry: Mostly dry: a gap with steep sides rather than a water obstacle.

dammedRivers.note: Rivers whose flow is held by dams or barrages (Indus Waters system, upstream in Pakistan or India). A river not in the list is read as undammed unless a dam, barrage or headworks on it lies within damSearchKm.

tank.src: OCOKA_Roadmap.md ch. 1 (Tank obstacle check, from IC / IBB); IC s85.4 (a ditch of 24 m is a full obstacle)

bridging.src: IBB Annex Q p467 (s1-2): bridge equipment of an infantry / armoured division and the spans it builds

spans.label: M2 Br (Cl 9)
spans.note: 84 m held by an Inf / Armd Div; 30 m in 1.3 h by day, 84 m in 2.25 h, 195 m in 4 h

spans.label: Hollow plate Br (Cl 50)
spans.note: 84 m held by an Armd Div; 30 m in 1.5 h, 84 m in 2.5 h, 168 m in 5 h by day

ford.note: Wading depths without preparation: a proposal, for the user to correct (Al-Khalid, wheeled B vehicles, a man with his kit).
